modifications: omlx transcribes the 'd' (M5 Ultra) plan with 128 partitions below 16K keys and refuses windows that straddle a plan; mlx2 computes every row's own plan with L3's select_sdpa_blocks transcription ('s' and 'd', every context) and runs one launch pair per run of rows sharing a plan, so windows straddling 1,024 / 8,192 / 32,768 keys are served.

omlx's dense arm is unmasked; mlx2's dense window is too (the one-token step's mask there is all-valid, the same arithmetic), and its masked arm adds a per-row boolean mask read from the rows' concatenated one-token masks (base offset computed in the kernel).

omlx batches projections/norms/appends and runs per-row scoring + selection + SDPA in its masked arm; mlx2 keeps each row's whole one-token forward (selection, QSA mask, append) and defers only the SDPA into one window launch, because mlx2's indexer state (index-key ledger cursor = cache offset) is row-sequential. Dense windows batch the index-key and K/V appends and the norm/RoPE launch after an admission check that runs before any state changes.
Rows up to 32 per window (copy drafts reach 17; omlx 16).
HC row-exact mode is mlx2-original: the L4 kernels' law 0 over grid rows, never qmv_wide, inside a window.
No omlx source text copied; no Apple copyright header added.
